Today every repository gets the same Repo dashboard, built for one shape of project (a frontend on one host and a backend on another). ticket.title: Connect repositories through a GitHub App instead of a pasted token and a hand-made webhook
ticket.body:
Today an organization's admin connects GitHub by hand: they create a fine-grained personal access token with the right permissions, paste it into Org settings › Integrations, then add a webhook in the repository's GitHub settings with a URL and a generated secret. That is fine for orgs onboarded by hand, and it is where setup will fail for orgs we don't know. A GitHub App would make Trov something an admin installs on their repositories.

## What it replaces

| | Today | With a GitHub App |

ticket.title: Let people create their own organization (self-serve org creation)
ticket.body:
Self-serve organization creation is switched off for now. Only a platform superadmin adds an organization (Platform › Add organization) and names its admin.

## The idea

Today every repository gets the same Repo dashboard, built for one shape of project (a frontend on one host and a backend on another). The idea is for Trov to look at a repository, work out how it is built and hosted, and propose a monitoring screen that fits it — and to let people accept that, pick a different layout, or adjust it.
